name: MATHVISTA
description: MATHVISTA is a benchmark designed to evaluate mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts. It consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA). The benchmark covers seven mathematical reasoning types (algebraic, arithmetic, geometry, logical, numeric common sense, scientific, and statistical reasoning) and five primary tasks (figure question answering, geometry problem solving, math word problem, textbook question answering, and visual question answering) across diverse visual contexts including natural images, geometry diagrams, abstract scenes, synthetic scenes, charts, and plots.
creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao (UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research)
citeAs: Lu, P., Bansal, H., Xia, T., Liu, J., Li, C., Hajishirzi, H., Cheng, H., Chang, K.-W., Galley, M., & Gao, J. MATHVISTA: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts.
rai:dataCollection: MATHVISTA was collected by: (1) collecting nine MathQA datasets in multimodal settings including GPS, MWP, and TQA datasets; (2) reviewing more than 70 VQA datasets and collecting 19 that contain math-related instances and are publicly available; (3) creating three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) to address gaps in logical reasoning on puzzle test figures, algebraic reasoning over functional plots, and scientific reasoning with academic paper figures. Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Only 85.6% of examples have annotations (5,261 out of 6,141). Annotations were sourced from original data providers, and due to the heterogeneity of these sources, annotations lack a unified format and structure.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Data was sourced from 28 existing multimodal datasets (9 MathQA datasets and 19 VQA datasets) and 3 newly created datasets. Sources include geometry problem datasets (Geometry3K, GeoQA+, GEOS, UniGeo), math word problem datasets (CLEVR-Math, IconQA, TabMWP), textbook QA datasets (SciBench, TheoremQA), and general VQA datasets (ChartQA, FigureQA, DVQA, MapQA, PlotQA, DocVQA, AI2D, ScienceQA, TQA, A-OKVQA, KVQA, ParsVQA-Caps, TextVQA, VizWiz, VQA2.0, PMC-VQA, VQA-RAD, Super-CLEVR, VQA-AS). IQTest examples were sourced from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms. PaperQA examples were sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: PaperQA examples were sourced from papers released in August 2023. Multimodal Bard was evaluated from Sep 8, 2023 to Sep 10, 2023. GPT-4V was evaluated from Oct 7, 2023 to Oct 15, 2023.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were designed to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning: examples with numeric answers or those containing quantity words in the questions were selected. This automatic filtration yielded 4,949 VQA-format examples. Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples. For the testmini subset, a sampling strategy was adopted: (1) randomly sample questions with a threshold number of 4 for each source dataset; (2) randomly sample the remaining questions for each source dataset based on its proportion in the entire set.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were used to automatically select math-related examples (numeric answers or quantity words in questions), yielding 4,949 candidates. Three expert annotators then manually labeled these examples to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning, using majority voting to finalize selections. Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples. The dataset was divided into testmini (1,000 examples) and test (5,141 examples) subsets. Several quality checks were conducted to address unidentified errors.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Multiple annotation processes were used: (1) For VQA mathematical reasoning labeling: three expert annotators manually labeled examples to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning, with majority voting used for final decisions. Annotators were given detailed instructions and examples. (2) For three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA): all questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and refined through a rigorous review process. Each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers, achieving 99.2% inter-annotation consistency. Discrepancies (6 out of 736 questions) were resolved through discussion. (3) For mathematical reasoning category labeling: expert annotators manually labeled 1,000 examples for mathematical reasoning categories from seven candidates, achieving 94.1% exact match with automatic annotations. (4) Human performance baseline: established using Amazon Mechanical Turk with annotators having high school diploma or higher, answering 5 questions within 20 minutes after passing qualification questions.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom annotation GUI tools (shown in Figures 22, 23, 24 in the paper) and Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) for human performance evaluation and Multimodal Bard assessment task.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotator agreement for VQA mathematical reasoning labeling was measured using Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775, indicating substantial consistency. For the three new datasets, inter-annotation consistency rate was 99.2% (only 6 out of 736 questions had disagreements). For automatic mathematical reasoning category annotation, 94.1% of examples had exact same set of reasoning types between automatic and human annotations, and 98.79% of individual labels were identical.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The answer labels for the test set will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination. An online evaluation platform will be maintained. The benchmark is part of an ongoing research process with commitment to maintaining datasets (refining potential data noise) in response to community feedback. The leaderboard will be evolved in response to new models.
rai:dataSocialImpact: MATHVISTA is designed to facilitate the development of AI agents capable of tackling mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks, with applications in educational disciplines, logical queries about statistical data, theorem proving, and scientific discovery. The benchmark highlights significant gaps between current AI models and human performance, underscoring the need for improvements in mathematical reasoning within visual contexts.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset's focus on mathematical reasoning within visual contexts spanning specific domains like science and college-level math may limit generalizability. The dataset coverage may have gaps in representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. Annotations were sourced from original data providers resulting in heterogeneous annotation formats. The benchmark features advanced topics such as college curricula and scientific reasoning, with human performance reaching only 60.3% accuracy, indicating high difficulty.
rai:dataLimitations: While MATHVISTA encompasses a broad spectrum of tasks and visual contexts, there may be gaps in representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. The dataset's focus on specific domains necessitates a more labor-intensive collection process, raising concerns about scalability and generalizability to other domains. Annotations lack a unified format and structure due to heterogeneous sources. Only 85.6% of examples have annotations. The benchmark focused exclusively on the most recent and prominent models at time of publication.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for evaluating (testing) mathematical reasoning capabilities of foundation models (LLMs and LMMs) in visual contexts. The testmini subset (1,000 examples) is intended for model development validation or for those with limited computing resources. The test set (5,141 examples) is for standard evaluation. The benchmark can also be used for fine-grained analysis across mathematical reasoning types, visual context types, task categories, and grade levels.
rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 annotators per item for VQA mathematical reasoning labeling and for the three new datasets; 5 annotators per item for human performance evaluation on testmini subset
rai:annotatorDemographics: For human performance evaluation: annotators from Amazon Mechanical Turk with more than 5,000 HIT tasks completed, acceptance score higher than 0.99, and high school diploma or higher. For new dataset annotation: graduate students in STEM fields. For VQA mathematical reasoning labeling: expert annotators trained with detailed instructions.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 (used as answer extractor with >99.5% accuracy on 200 examples); EasyOCR (JaidedAI, 2020) for OCR text detection; Multimodal Bard for image caption generation; automatic heuristic rules for selecting math-related VQA examples based on numeric answers or quantity words
